title: Discovery: Cost/unit economics - Helios Finance
summary: Intro + qualification focused on per-token economics, budget constraints, and deployment choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private). SE dug into batching/caching levers and expected throughput; customer asked for pricing examples and benchmarking next steps.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next steps: pricing spreadsheet and benchmark run
action_items: Maya: Send pricing worksheet with sample per-token calc and Hosted vs Dedicated examples (due 2025-05-09)
Carlos: Share recommended batching & cache config for Helios query distribution (due 2025-05-12)
Avery: Provide sample prompt set and expected QPS for pilot (due 2025-05-13)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing worksheet and runbook for pilot
Schedule 1-hr benchmark session with Helios infra team (Carlos + Jordan)
Helios to share prompt set and data residency requirements
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 44m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Avery (Head of ML - Helios), Jordan (Infra Lead - Helios), Sana (CTO - Helios)

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intro from me and carlos. we're the account team at Redwood, i'm maya AE, carlos is our solutions engineer.
00:18 Avery (Helios): hi yep thanks, i'm avery, running applied ml at Helios. we're exploring options for LLM infra, cost is the big thing for us.
00:30 Carlos (Redwood SE): great. quick agenda - walk through your current usage, talk about per-token economics, batching and caching levers, and then deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) and security.
00:48 Jordan (Helios): sounds good. for context we're doing re-ranking and some generation in product, roughly 12M tokens/day now, spikey QPS during mornings.
01:05 Maya: perfect - can you share ballpark budget? helps us tailor hosted vs dedicated recommendations.
01:14 Sana (Helios): we have a budget envelope of about $25k/month for inference initially, could expand if ROI is clear.
01:25 Carlos: ok that's useful. to orient: our Hosted API pricing is per-token - baseline examples we usually show: inference only generation X n cents/token depending on model. Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity - better for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale because of GPU amortization.
01:52 Avery: can you give a concrete calc? like if we're doing 12M tokens/day where does that land?
02:02 Carlos: sure quick napkin - 12M tokens/day ~ 360M tokens/month. on Hosted with a mid-sized open model let's say $0.0006/token (example), that'd be ~ $216k/month, obviously above your $25k. with Dedicated, you reserve capacity - effective unit costs can drop 3-8x depending on batch and caching. so that can get you into the $25-60k range typically.
02:40 Maya: caveat that numbers vary by model family and quantization; we can run an exact calc if you share prompt lengths and percent cache hit.
02:55 Jordan: prompt lengths are average 60 tokens, responses 140 tokens. we have lots of repeated prefixes for re-ranking - could caching help?
03:08 Carlos: yes, prefix/KV caching is big for re-ranking. if you get 40-60% prefix cache hit, token compute drops considerably. plus batching improves GPU utilization - but there's a latency tradeoff.
03:30 Avery: latency SLO is 300ms p95 for interactive features, background batch can be higher.
03:39 Carlos: with dedicated and smart batching you can meet 200-400ms p95 for many models. for Hosted we have multi-tiered routing; for strict p95 < 200ms it might be safer to go Dedicated or private.
04:05 Sana: what about private deployments - we have data residency constraints and need VPC + KMS.
04:14 Maya: Redwood Private supports VPC and customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and on-prem if needed. pricing includes a platform license + infra. it's more capex but gives control and solves residency.
04:36 Jordan: any SOC2 / compliance stuff we should see?
04:41 Maya: yes we are SOC 2 Type II and can share the report under NDA. also SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported.
04:53 Avery: back to cost - you mentioned model/quantization; how much savings with int8/4-bit?
05:01 Carlos: quantization can cut memory and perf per token; 4-bit/8-bit can reduce cost ~20-50% depending on model ops. combined with batching and caching might reach ~5-10x effective unit improvement compared to naive hosted calls.
05:28 Maya: also recommendation: for early pilot start Hosted with a small throughput and collect cache/hits then evaluate Dedicated if predictable.
05:36 Avery: that seems like our prefered path - pilot hosted, measure, then reserved. budget needs to be respected.
05:43 Jordan: curious about burst policies with dedicated - if we need short spikes above reserved capacity what happens?
05:50 Carlos: we have configurable burst pools and autoscale policies; you can set a burst budget or fallback to lower-capacity model variants. costs for burst are metered; we'll show typical configs.
06:05 Maya: i'll share a pricing worksheet with scenarios: hosted-only, dedicated-reserved, private-license - with sample per-token math given your tokens/day and prompt lengths.
06:18 Sana: great. any transparency on token accounting? we need token-level cost per route for engineering.
06:23 Carlos: Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, and cost attribution, and you can tag routes for chargeback.
06:35 Avery: ok good. can you run a quick benchmark with our prompt set? we'd like latency + cost numbers.
06:41 Maya: yes, next step - you share prompt set, we'll schedule a benchmark window. carlos will run it and produce a config recommendation.
06:50 Jordan: good. on network side we want to validate KV cache and also how stateful KV is handled across nodes.
06:58 Carlos: KV cache is sharded and persists across requests in dedicated and private. for hosted we have an ephemeral cache with prefix caching options; we'll document consistency model.
07:14 Avery: any gotchas re: model variants when falling back to cheaper models? we don't want quality regressions.
07:22 Carlos: we support canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback policies that prefer quality; we'll link our eval harness to monitor quality regressions on your prompt set.
07:37 Sana: competitors - we're also talking to OpenAI and Anthropic and a smaller infra vendor FortressAI. how do you compare on unit cost?
07:48 Maya: high-level: OpenAI's hosted price is competitive but locked to their model families; our advantage is model catalog + runtime levers to tune cost. vs Anthropic similar. FortressAI pitched lower price but needed more ops work. we'll include a competitor comparison doc.
08:05 Avery: transcription is a bit fuzzy but that's fine.
08:10 Maya: quick demo snippet from carlos on batching math - carlos?
08:14 Carlos: yep - take GPU throughput, say you can do N tokens/sec at batch size 32 vs 8, efficiency scales sublinearly; we typically see 2-3x throughput improvement from batching alone. combined with caching that stacks.
08:36 Jordan: but batching increases latency for single requests right?
08:40 Carlos: yes so you tune queueing windows and priority lanes; interactive routes get smaller batch windows.
08:49 Avery: what's a realistic latency increase at our p95 if we push batching?
08:53 Carlos: depends - small batch windows add ~20-80ms; large windows increase more. with our suggested config for 300ms p95 you can still batch moderately.
09:10 Maya: i'll include example configs for latency-sensitive vs throughput-optimized routes.
09:17 Sana: we'd like to see cost per 1000 tokens comparisons across models with and without caching.
09:23 Maya: noted.
09:27 Carlos: quick note on golden prompts - if you can surface high-signal prompts we'll target caching there for biggest wins.
09:36 Avery: we can supply.
09:40 Jordan: timeline wise we want a pilot in the next 3-4 weeks. is that feasible?
09:46 Maya: yes - pilot 2-4 weeks typical. we'll need prompt set and QPS windows.
09:52 Carlos: we'll propose pilot scope: two routes (interactive + re-rank), benchmark baseline on Hosted, then run Dedicated estimate.
10:05 Avery: pricing cap - we can't exceed $35k in first month of pilot ideally.
10:11 Maya: we can size pilot to hit that cap; might restrict tokens or run sampling.
10:18 Sana: send a clear pilot SOW.
10:21 Carlos: will do, including expected metrics and telemetry we'll collect.
10:28 Maya: ok let's recap next steps - i'll send pricing worksheet, carlos will prepare batching/cache config and run benchmarks, avery to send prompt set, and we schedule the benchmark.
10:44 Avery: thanks everyone.
10:47 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up by friday with docs.
10:51 Sana: bye.

(End of transcript)
